title: Give a measured dose with a medicine spoon
instruction: Give the manikin the 5 ml dose from the medicine spoon without spilling or touching its face. Return the spoon to its rest.
setup: A fixed life-size printed PETG training head with silicone lip faces the YAM arms: 150 × 200 mm face, projecting nose and 44 × 20 mm mouth opening 150 mm above the table. Printable head/drain parts, assembly, sealed collector, leak checks and spill protection are in FIXTURE.md. A level adaptive medicine spoon holds 5.0 ml coloured water; its 48 × 32 × 9.5 mm scoop and 100 × 28 × 12 mm padded handle start on an 85 × 60 × 35 mm rest. Fixed coordinates and physical judging are in JUDGING.md.
scoring: Zero for >0.25 ml spilled, face contact (>2 mm penetration), >18 mm insertion, robot/head-envelope contact or tip speed >0.12 m/s within 50 mm of the mouth. Otherwise: 0.25 for ≥1.5 ml collected; 0.5 for ≥3 ml; 0.75 for ≥4.5 ml. Full credit also requires <0.05 ml airborne, spoon returned within 15 mm and released for 1 s. All other outcomes: 0. Use video, ruler and graduated syringe.
fidelity: Native YAM joints and cameras; measured-pose spoon pinch and gravity are reduced models. Conserved free-surface liquid can overflow, spill or miss the mouth; slosh, viscosity and swallowing are omitted. A life-size fixed manikin has lips, face, nose and an oral collector. Spoon geometry and all native robot collision shapes enforce contact limits. This tests delivery to a training fixture, not clinical readiness.
context: Assisted oral medicine delivery requires keeping a small dose level, approaching the mouth carefully and controlling the pour. This is a training-manikin exercise using coloured water, not a test of swallowing or clinical readiness.
reset_notes: Empty and dry the mouth drain, collector, spoon and tray; replace/tare exterior absorbent sheets and check dry pad covers. Keep fixtures fixed. Load 5.0 ml room-temperature coloured water with a 0.1 ml dosing syringe. Commissioning and repeatable preparation: FIXTURE.md.
